name: io.github.ravidsrk/slop-detect-mcp
description: MCP server that scores any landing page against the AI-design-slop fingerprint (deterministic 0-100, real Chromium), copy tells, DESIGN.md system compliance, and AEO technical eligibility, and builds remediation prompts.

transport.notes: Local stdio MCP server (npm: slop-detect-mcp) or zero-install remote Streamable HTTP endpoint at https://slop-detect.com/mcp.

tools.name: scan_page
tools.title: Scan Page for Default-Template Patterns
tools.description: Score a landing page against the versioned default-template pattern catalogue. The design axis inspects computed CSS and DOM in headless Chromium; add the copy axis for prose tells, the craft axis for a separate defect floor, and design_md_url to also score compliance with the site's DESIGN.md. Use it when the user asks whether a page looks generic or templated, wants a slop score, or before and after UI changes. Returns a short summary: score 0–100 (lower is better; Clean 0–9, Mild 10–27, Heavy 28+), tier, grade, and only the triggered patterns with their IDs, weights and evidence. Each call runs a real browser scan (about 5–30 seconds); hosted scans are rate limited per IP. localhost and file:// URLs need the npm server started with --local. Results are not published anywhere. Scores measure overlap with common template defaults, not who or what made the page. Not for crawler or AI-engine readiness (check_aeo) or for linting a DESIGN.md file (lint_design_md). Next step: fix_prompt with the scan_id (npm server) or the triggered pattern IDs.

tools.name: check_aeo
tools.title: Check AEO Crawler & Citation Readiness
tools.description: Check whether search engines and AI answer engines can fetch, parse and cite a page, using static HTTP checks (no browser): reachability, edge access, robots.txt search rules, indexability, AI preview controls, server-rendered text coverage, a Markdown twin, llms.txt and more. Use it when the user asks whether ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity or search crawlers can read or cite their site. Returns a 0–100 score where higher is better, a tier (Eligible 80+, Partially Eligible 50–79, Restricted below 50) and the failed checks. Takes a few seconds. The scanner uses its own user agent and doesn't impersonate vendor crawlers, so a site that blocks unknown bots can score lower than real crawlers would see it. localhost needs the npm server started with --local; file:// pages can't be checked. Not for visual or copy quality (scan_page).

tools.name: check_design_system
tools.title: Check DESIGN.md System Compliance
tools.description: Check whether a live page follows its own declared design system: a DESIGN.md (Google Labs format) or a W3C DTCG tokens.json. Use it before shipping UI changes on a site that publishes a DESIGN.md, to catch fonts, CTA and surface colours, and radii that drift from the declared tokens. Returns a 0–100 compliance score where higher is better (Aligned 80+, Drifting 50–79, Off-system below 50) and the named drift signals; if the site declares no system it says so instead of scoring. Runs a browser scan (about 5–30 seconds) unless scan_id points at an earlier scan_page result that included design_md_url. If you already called scan_page with design_md_url, its response already contains this result. Unlike scan_page, it judges the page against the site's own tokens, not against template defaults.

tools.name: fix_prompt
tools.title: Build Remediation Prompt
tools.description: Build a copy-paste remediation prompt for a coding agent: for each triggered pattern, what was found, why it reads as a template default, the fix, alternatives and a hard rule, plus the heaviest currently-passing patterns not to introduce. Use it after scan_page when the user wants the findings fixed. Reuse the scan you already have: pass scan_id (npm server) or patterns (the triggered pattern IDs from scan_page). Pass url only when there is no scan yet; that runs a new browser scan (about 5–30 seconds). brief: true returns a short avoid list (at most 120 words) instead; with no url, scan_id or patterns it returns a generic avoid list for a page that has not been built yet. Returns text only; it doesn't edit files.

tools.name: lint_design_md
tools.title: Lint a DESIGN.md File
tools.description: Statically lint DESIGN.md text: broken token references, component contrast below WCAG 4.5:1, orphaned palette tokens, and a specVersion other than alpha. Use it while writing or editing a DESIGN.md. Local and instant: it doesn't fetch a page and doesn't change any score. Pass the document text, not a path or URL (read the file first). Returns valid or invalid, error and warning counts, and each issue with its rule ID and token path.

tools.name: diff_design_md
tools.title: Diff Two DESIGN.md Files
tools.description: Compare two DESIGN.md documents token by token and list added, removed and changed tokens; a removed or changed token is breaking. Use it when reviewing a change to a DESIGN.md. Local and instant: it doesn't fetch or rescore a page. Pass both documents as text (read the files first).

tools.name: extract_design_system
tools.title: Extract DESIGN.md & DTCG Tokens from a Page
tools.description: Reverse-engineer a starter design system from a live page: the colours, typography, radii, shadows and spacing it renders become a Google Labs DESIGN.md and/or a W3C DTCG 2025.10 tokens.json. Use it to bootstrap a DESIGN.md for a site that has none. Runs a browser scan of url (about 5–30 seconds) unless you pass scan_id (an earlier scan_page made with design_md_url; npm server only) or observed tokens. The output describes what the page renders today, not a recommended palette; review it before publishing. Returns the document text; it doesn't write files.

resources.name: Slop Detector Editorial-Instrument Score Card (MCP App)

prompts.name: audit_landing_page
prompts.description: Run the design, copy and AEO checks on a URL (plus DESIGN.md compliance when the site has one) and write a prioritized report.

prompts.name: deslop_and_verify
prompts.description: Build the fix prompt for a page, apply the fixes in the codebase, then re-scan where the changes run to confirm the result.

prompts.name: refactor_to_design_system
prompts.description: Check a page against its DESIGN.md, fix the drifting components, and re-check.
